_why: THE DOCUMENTED LIST IS DERIVED FROM TRAFFIC, NOT ASSERTED AT IT (Zac, 2026-09-20). The list in request-taxonomy.js field 8 was hand-written: it named six languages nobody had ever typed (id, ja, ko, nl, zh, ta-en) and omitted seven that people had (fr, fa, bn, he, pl, tr, ur = 9 of 101 rows, 8.9%). A list written from assumption is a prior pointing the model away from what its users actually write.
_note: Counts span the vocabulary seam at 5800071 and are normalized to BCP-47 by lib/language-tag.js, so `English` (79) and `en` (6) are ONE bucket of 85.
_not_closed: typed_in is {type:'string'}, never an enum. A language not here MUST be written as its own tag rather than forced into one of these — the list is what has been SEEN, not what is allowed.
_extra_why: `mixed` is a real answer the model needs and is not a language, so it sits beside the derived tags rather than inside them.
